subject.title: [Feature]: Make the control-plane write rate limit configurable

question: Should gateways be allowed to globally raise the shipped per-identity control-plane write budget, and is the proposed 1–600 range an acceptable security boundary?
rationale: The setting changes a security control protecting privileged config and update RPCs and adds permanent gateway configuration; implementation tests cannot determine the acceptable operator-controlled ceiling or whether global scope is the intended product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded setting
options.body: Accept the linked PR direction while preserving the default and requiring explicit documentation and tests for the global security impact.

options.title: Require narrower trust scoping
options.body: Ask for a trusted automation or auth-class mechanism so unrelated identities retain the fixed budget.

options.title: Retain the fixed budget
options.body: Decline configurability and document pacing, batching, or coalescing expectations for provisioning systems.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded setting
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR direction while preserving the default and requiring explicit documentation and tests for the global security impact.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes a shipped gateway security default and permanent core configuration surface, aligning with project-direction ownership.
